shell.draftNotice: Test version. This questionnaire is not evaluated yet.
shell.incomplete: You do not have to commit to anything: for every question you can also state that it is still open or that you would rather not answer it. {count} answers are still missing.
shell.submitted: Submitted. Nothing here can be changed from now on.
shell.submitHint: Afterwards you can go through your answers and mark what you want to talk about.

step1.title: Part one
step1.intro: This is about how you want to work, what you want to achieve and which rules you would like — not about who you are.
step1.note: There are no better or worse answers and no score at the end. The questionnaire saves as you go; you can stop anytime and continue later.

step2.title: Part two: the commitments
step2.intro: Now it is about hours, money and dates. These are commitments, not self-description — which is why they come later.
step2.note: Everything here describes where you stand today. It is not an obligation, and you can change it later.

values.title: Priorities and limits
values.intro: Short situations in which two reasonable concerns collide. You say separately how important each one is to you — both may be very important.
values.note: There is no right choice and no evaluation of your values. The point is to know what you should talk about.
values.concerns: How important is each of these two concerns to you?
values.pathQuestion: Which way would you choose first under these conditions?

missing.heading: Or:
missing.hint: This counts as an answer. It is not a skip.

sourceLanguage: The questions themselves are shown in German. Translating a measurement instrument is not a translation task but a re-validation: an item that reads differently measures something else, and none of the equivalence work has been done. An English version comes after the cognitive interviews, not before.

discussion.mark: I want to talk about this
discussion.markHint: It then goes to the top of your conversation agenda — even if you both answered the same.

report.title: Your answers
report.intro: This is not an assessment of you. It prepares the conversation that still lies ahead.
report.openIntro: This is the most useful part: exactly here is where you would talk.
report.emptyIntro: Once you have filled in the questionnaire, your answers appear here — sorted and without any rating.
report.orphans: For {count, plural, =1 {one question} other {# questions}} there is an answer below that refers to a limit you have since removed. It is not deleted — you can leave it as it is or overwrite it in the questionnaire.
report.unreadable: This answer cannot be read. That is a fault on our side — it is saved and not lost.

maps.workIntro: Your answers side by side — one dot per answer, at the position you chose, with no section value. This is the same as below, only more compact. Questions without an order appear below only.
maps.differenceIntro: Only the questions you both answered and that have an order. A wide gap does not mean something is wrong — it means you have not talked about it yet.
maps.directionIntro: Six goals side by side, each with the weight you gave it. They are not added up — none comes at the cost of another, and there is no total.

advisor.visible: You see {count} of {of} questions. What is missing may be withheld or unanswered — from here the two cannot be told apart.

compare.title: The two of you
compare.intro: Side by side, not calculated against each other. There is no fit score and no rating here.
compare.cardsIntro: At most four topics per conversation. Everything else is below for reference.
compare.nothingYet: Nothing to discuss yet — or answers are still missing.
compare.agreementHint: You set the amounts and deadlines, not the questionnaire.
compare.question: Question

transition.title: There is a new version of the questionnaire
transition.intro: The questionnaire has been reworked: better questions, separate reasons for leaving something out, and no score at the end. You decide what happens to your existing answers.
transition.reversible: You can change this later. Your old answers are kept either way.

confirmed.keep_previous: Your existing report stays valid. You can answer again at any time.
confirmed.retake: Done — your old answers are kept, and the new questionnaire is waiting.

discovery.title: What matters to you in the search
discovery.intro: You state a wish per topic. This does not produce a fit score — it produces an order that you set yourself.
discovery.orderIntro: Your first topic is looked at first. The second only breaks a tie. Someone who does not fit your most important topic is not lifted by matches further down.
discovery.nothingChosen: No topic chosen yet. Pick what matters to you below.
discovery.verdictTitle: Your search settings, applied to this person
discovery.verdictIntro: In your order. There is deliberately no overall number here.

synthesis.title: What shows in your answers
synthesis.intro: Put together from the answers you gave — question by question. Where your answers within a theme pull apart, that is what it says.
synthesis.tooFew: There are not enough answers here yet for a connected description.
synthesis.note: The descriptions summarise your answers; they are not a diagnosis, not a comparison against a norm and not a score.

shortLabels.I01: first impression in a familiar field
shortLabels.I02: gut feeling when options look equal

weighing.title: Weighing decisions
weighing.low: Before you commit, you rarely compare systematically and rarely check an assumption on purpose.
weighing.middle: Comparing and checking are part of how you decide — but not with every decision.
weighing.high: Before you commit, you compare the options and check what speaks for your assumptions.

experience.title: Experience & gut feeling
experience.low: You do not automatically treat your first impression or your gut feeling as a basis for deciding.
experience.middle: Experience and gut feeling count for you without being decisive.
experience.high: You give your experience and your gut feeling clear weight when you decide.

trying.title: Trying things & learning
trying.low: Trying something out before thinking it through further is not really your way.
trying.middle: Trying things out happens with you, but it is not the first move.
trying.high: Where something can be tried out, you tend to do that rather than think further.

openQuestions.title: Living with open questions
openQuestions.low: When something stays open, you tend to find that uncomfortable.
openQuestions.middle: You can live with open situations without being comfortable in them.
openQuestions.high: You get on well with situations that stay open.

A01.low: You rarely compare several options systematically before you commit.
A01.middle: You sometimes compare the options before you commit.
A01.high: With several options in front of you, you usually weigh their pros and cons before you commit.

A02.low: You rarely check on purpose whether an important assumption holds.
A02.middle: You sometimes check on purpose whether an important assumption holds.
A02.high: When a decision rests on an assumption, you usually check what speaks for and against it.

I01.low: In fields you know well, your first impression carries little weight.
I01.middle: In fields you know well, your first impression counts for something.
I01.high: In fields you know well, your first impression carries a lot of weight.

I02.low: When several options look about equally good, you give your experience little weight.
I02.middle: When several options look about equally good, your experience counts for something.
I02.high: When several options look about equally good, experience tends to decide it for you.

I03.low: When the numbers favour one option and your gut says otherwise, you tend to follow the numbers.
I03.middle: When the numbers favour one option and your gut says otherwise, you take the feeling partly as a signal.
I03.high: When numbers and gut feeling pull against each other, you clearly take the feeling as an extra signal.

E01.low: Before testing, you tend to research further.
E01.middle: Whether you test first or research further depends on the situation for you.
E01.high: You like small tests when they bring new information faster than more research would.

E02.low: Trying two paths in parallel on a small scale is not really your way.
E02.middle: Trying two paths in parallel does happen with you.
E02.high: When two paths both look sensible, you tend to try both on a small scale rather than commit at once.

E03.low: Even with easily reversible decisions, you tend not to settle on a provisional direction.
E03.middle: With easily reversible decisions, you sometimes settle on a provisional direction.
E03.high: When a decision is easy to reverse, you tend to set a provisional direction already.

D02.low: You tend not to say outright that you do not agree with a proposal.
D02.middle: Whether you say outright that you do not agree depends on the situation for you.
D02.high: When a proposal does not seem sound to you, you tend to say outright that you do not agree.

X01.low: Several plausible explanations for one result tend to make you uncomfortable.
X01.middle: You can live with several plausible explanations side by side.
X01.high: Several plausible explanations for one result are something you are comfortable with.

X02.low: Weeks of uncertainty about which direction the venture takes tend to make you uncomfortable.
X02.middle: You can live with a direction that stays open for weeks.
X02.high: Weeks of uncertainty about which direction the venture takes are something you get on with.

X03.low: Conflicting feedback on the same idea tends to make you uncomfortable.
X03.middle: You can live with conflicting feedback on the same idea.
X03.high: You take conflicting feedback on the same idea calmly.

X04.low: An important question staying unanswered for a while tends to make you uncomfortable.
X04.middle: You can live with an important question staying unanswered for a while.
X04.high: An important question staying unanswered for a while is something you are comfortable with.

T01.0: You raise an objection to an important decision while the conversation is still going.
T01.1: You raise an objection after the conversation, but on the same working day.
T01.2: You raise an objection the next working day.
T01.3: You raise an objection once more than a working day has passed.
T01.4: When you raise an objection depends on the situation for you.

T02.0: Concerns you cannot name precisely yet, you raise directly and say that they are still unclear.
T02.1: Concerns you cannot name precisely yet, you mention briefly and come back to in more detail later.
T02.2: Concerns you cannot name precisely yet, you sort out for yourself first and then raise.
T02.3: You raise concerns once you can name them fairly precisely.
T02.4: How you handle concerns that are still unclear depends on the situation for you.

D01.0: When you disagree, you are most likely to say so directly: „I see that differently, because …“
D01.1: When you disagree, you are most likely to name your concerns: „I still have reservations on that point …“
D01.2: When you disagree, you are most likely to ask how the proposal would deal with your objection.
D01.3: When you disagree, you are most likely to bring another option into play.
D01.4: None of the offered wordings fits how you disagree.
